name: Workforce Pell Grants — Short-Term Career Training
description: Beginning July 1, 2026, the expanded Workforce Pell Grants allow students from low-income families — including lawful permanent residents and eligible immigrants — to use federal Pell Grant funds for short-term career training programs as brief as eight weeks. Eligible learners can receive up to $4,310 per year toward credentialed programs in high-demand fields such as information technology, health care, and skilled trades. Programs must lead to recognized industry credentials, certifications, or licenses and be offered by eligible postsecondary institutions. This expansion addresses the gap between traditional degree programs and workforce needs, making career-focused education accessible to immigrants seeking rapid entry into the U.S. job market.
eligibility: U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and eligible non-citizens with demonstrated financial need; must be enrolled in an eligible short-term credentialed program at a participating postsecondary institution; standard Pell Grant eligibility criteria apply including FAFSA completion
applicationProcess: Complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at studentaid.gov. Enroll in an eligible short-term career training program at a participating postsecondary institution. The institution's financial aid office will determine Pell Grant eligibility and disburse funds. Programs must be at least eight weeks long and lead to a recognized credential.
geographicScope: United States — all states and territories with participating institutions
documentsRequired: FAFSA application, Social Security number or eligible non-citizen documentation, federal tax returns or income information, high school diploma or equivalent, enrollment in eligible program

name: Canada Foreign Credential Recognition Program
description: The Foreign Credential Recognition (FCR) Program helps internationally trained professionals get their credentials assessed and recognized in Canada so they can work in their field. With $97 million in new funding over five years starting in 2026–2027, the program maintains 58 agreements supporting approximately 32,000 internationally trained professionals annually. The program focuses primarily on health care and construction sectors but covers many regulated professions. Services include financial support through specialized loans, mentorship, job readiness training, employment assistance, and direct support for credential assessment processes. For immigrants arriving in Canada with professional qualifications, this program is a critical pathway to working in their trained profession rather than accepting underemployment.
eligibility: Internationally trained professionals (ITPs) residing in Canada, including permanent residents, refugees, and newcomers; must hold professional qualifications from outside Canada; priority given to health care and construction sector professionals
amount: Varies by province and profession — includes loans, assessment fee coverage, and bridging program funding
applicationProcess: Contact your provincial or territorial credential assessment body to begin the recognition process. Apply through ESDC-funded partner organizations in your province. Some professions have specific regulatory bodies that manage the assessment. Financial support is accessed through program partner organizations. Visit canada.ca/foreign-credential-recognition for province-specific guidance.
documentsRequired: Original professional credentials and transcripts, certified translations of documents not in English or French, proof of Canadian residency status, professional references, proof of work experience in trained profession

name: Germany Recognition Grant (Anerkennungszuschuss)
organization: Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF)
description: The German Recognition Grant (Anerkennungszuschuss) provides financial support of up to €600 to help immigrants and refugees in Germany pay for their foreign qualification recognition procedures. The grant covers costs of the recognition process including fees for credential assessment, document translations, certifications, and required aptitude tests. Since 2005, Germany has established a comprehensive system for recognizing foreign professional qualifications, and this grant removes the financial barrier that prevents many immigrants from completing the process. Recognition of foreign qualifications is essential for immigrants to work in their trained profession in Germany, particularly in regulated professions such as medicine, nursing, engineering, and teaching.
eligibility: Immigrants and refugees residing in Germany with foreign professional qualifications; low-income individuals who cannot afford recognition costs; must have already initiated or plan to initiate a recognition procedure under the German Recognition Act (Anerkennungsgesetz)
applicationProcess: Apply through the hotline 'Working and Living in Germany' (phone: +49 30 1815-1111) or through local counseling centers for recognition (Anerkennungsberatungsstellen). Counselors will assess eligibility and help with the application. The grant is paid directly toward recognition procedure costs. Applications can be submitted before or during the recognition process.
documentsRequired: Foreign professional qualification certificates, proof of residence in Germany, proof of low income or benefit receipt, cost estimate from the recognition authority, identification document

name: Upwardly Global — Professional Career Services for Immigrants
description: Upwardly Global provides free professional career services to help immigrants, refugees, and asylees rebuild their careers in the United States. The program serves internationally trained professionals who face barriers to employment in their fields due to credential recognition gaps, lack of U.S. work experience, and unfamiliarity with American hiring practices. Services include individualized career coaching, resume and LinkedIn optimization for the U.S. job market, interview preparation, professional networking opportunities, skills-based job matching, and connections with hiring partners across industries. Since its founding, Upwardly Global has helped thousands of immigrant professionals secure jobs matching their skills and experience, with an average salary increase of 300% compared to their initial U.S. employment.
eligibility: Immigrants, refugees, asylees, and Special Immigrant Visa holders authorized to work in the United States; must have professional-level education or experience from outside the U.S.; English proficiency sufficient for professional work
amount: Free program — no cost to participants
applicationProcess: Apply online at upwardlyglobal.org. Complete the intake questionnaire and submit your resume. If accepted, you are matched with a career coach and begin the job readiness program. The program typically runs 4-8 weeks with ongoing support until employment is secured.
geographicScope: United States — services available nationwide (virtual and in-person in select cities)
documentsRequired: Resume or CV, proof of work authorization in the U.S., professional credentials from home country (if available)

name: Maryland New American Workforce Program — Education & Training Scholarships
organization: Maryland Department of Labor — Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning
description: The Maryland New American Workforce Program provides education and training scholarships specifically for immigrants and refugees settling in Maryland. The program funds English language training, vocational skills courses, professional certification preparation, and workforce readiness programs. Scholarships cover tuition, fees, books, and training materials at approved educational institutions and training providers throughout Maryland. The program is part of Maryland's broader workforce development strategy to help new Americans achieve economic self-sufficiency through skills development and credentialing. Participants also receive case management, career counseling, and job placement support.
eligibility: Immigrants, refugees, and asylees residing in Maryland; must be authorized to work in the United States; must demonstrate need for education or training to obtain employment or advance career; priority given to those with limited English proficiency or foreign credentials requiring U.S. equivalency
amount: Varies — covers tuition, fees, books, and training materials for approved programs
applicationProcess: Contact a Maryland American Job Center or the Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning to begin the application process. An intake assessment determines eligibility and appropriate training programs. Approved applicants are enrolled in selected education or training programs with scholarship funding.
documentsRequired: Proof of identity, proof of work authorization, proof of Maryland residency, educational background documentation, income verification

name: New American Pathways — Refugee Workforce Development Program
description: New American Pathways offers comprehensive workforce development services for refugees and immigrants in the greater Atlanta, Georgia area. The program includes job skills training, vocational ESL classes, financial literacy education, asset building workshops, and direct job placement assistance. Their Economic Inclusion program specifically addresses employment challenges faced by refugees including language barriers, unfamiliarity with U.S. workplace culture, and foreign qualification recognition. The organization partners with local employers to create job pipelines in growing industries such as hospitality, manufacturing, health care support, and logistics. Participants receive individualized employment plans and ongoing support for up to two years after initial placement.
eligibility: Refugees, asylees, Special Immigrant Visa holders, Cuban/Haitian entrants, and victims of trafficking residing in the Atlanta metropolitan area; must be authorized to work in the U.S.
amount: Free program — includes training, ESL classes, and job placement services at no cost
applicationProcess: Contact New American Pathways directly or visit their Atlanta office. Complete an intake assessment to determine service needs. You will be assigned a case manager who develops an individualized employment plan. Training and job placement services begin based on the plan.
documentsRequired: Immigration status documentation, work authorization, proof of residence in Atlanta area, identification

name: Germany BOFplus — Vocational Preparation for Immigrants
organization: Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF)
description: The BOFplus programme (Berufsorientierung für Geflüchtete plus) prepares newly arrived immigrants and refugees in Germany for entry into the German vocational training system (Berufsausbildung). The program runs until the end of 2027 and offers intensive courses combining vocational orientation, German language instruction focused on professional terminology, and hands-on practical training in workshops. Participants explore various vocational fields, receive guidance on the German apprenticeship system, and are supported in finding training placements with employers. The program bridges the gap between general integration courses and formal vocational training, which is the primary pathway to skilled employment in Germany. All costs including course fees and materials are covered by federal funding.
eligibility: Refugees and immigrants residing in Germany with completed compulsory schooling; must have at least B1-level German language skills; must be seeking entry into the German vocational training system; open to asylum seekers with good prospects of remaining
amount: Fully funded — course fees, materials, and supervision costs covered by the federal government
applicationProcess: Apply through local BAMF offices, migration counseling services (Migrationsberatung), or career guidance centers (Berufsinformationszentren). Participants undergo an aptitude assessment and language level check. Accepted participants are placed in a BOFplus course at a participating training center. The program typically lasts 6 to 12 months.
geographicScope: Germany — participating training centers in all federal states
documentsRequired: Proof of residence in Germany, immigration status documentation, B1 German language certificate, school completion certificate (or equivalent), identification document
